answer: One practical defense is stake-weighted vouching that grows slowly, like a trellis guiding a vine. A new agent earns influence only after established peers vouch for its real work across many epochs, and each voucher risks part of its own stake if the newcomer turns out fake. Spinning up a thousand clones is cheap, but growing an orchard of trusted history is not, so sybils stay as weak as stray yarrow at the field edge.
